query: Our Node.js CLI uses minimist@1.2.5 to parse user-provided arguments. Can we continue using this version in production? Check known vulnerabilities and recommend a safe alternative or patched version.
answer:
Target:   unknown (package: minimist, npm) · minimist@1.2.5 · checked 2026-11-21
Decision: 🔴 Do not adopt

No, do not keep minimist 1.2.5 in production. It has a critical known flaw that is fixed in 1.2.6,
so upgrade to 1.2.6 or newer. Licence and maintenance could not be verified because the repo lookup
failed.

Why
 🔴 Security: 1.2.5 has a critical prototype pollution advisory, fixed in 1.2.6. (CRA Art. 13(5))
   • Version 1.2.5 has a critical vulnerability (GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h / CVE-2021-44906); fixed in
     1.2.6, 0.2.4.
     "Prototype Pollution in minimist" → https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h ✔
   • Version 1.2.5 has a known critical flaw (prototype pollution, CVE-2021-44906). Crafted input
     can alter an app's internal objects, which can lead to crashes or changed behaviour. Fixed in
     1.2.6.
     "Prototype Pollution in minimist" → https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h ✔
   🔴 1.2.5: critical vulnerability GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h / CVE-2021-44906; fixed in 1.2.6, 0.2.4

What to do next
 1. Upgrade minimist to 1.2.6 or newer (0.2.4 or newer if you are on the 0.x line) and re-run your
   tests.
 2. Run 'npm ls minimist' to find copies pulled in by other packages, and force the patched version
   with npm 'overrides'.
 3. Verify the licence and maintenance status of minimist manually before sign-off, since the repo
   check failed.

Limitations
 • Licence not checked: repo substack/minimist: not found (404) - check the spelling
 • Open question: Is minimist a direct dependency, or pulled in by other packages (check your
   lockfile)?

Not checked: maintenance, privacy, skills
